items.title: What Kind of Aftermath Is This?: three terms said where they're used
items.where: What Kind of Aftermath Is This?, list item
items.comment: link somatic experiencing to my guide at somatic.u-dont-exist.com
items.my_version:
Anxiety and fear: with this pattern, it helps to first figure out what is providing the stimulation for the anxiety. CBT-style reality testing, checking the frightening thought against what's actually happening, is one way to do that which could be explored with a therapist if it persists, but can be done without one to start with. In general, it can help to have grounding/relaxing routines (like morning or bedtime yin yoga, meeting a friend for lunch).

Derealization and depersonalization (when the world, or you yourself, feel unreal): Is it due to isolation? Rumination (which often goes along with isolation)? Peer and family support are crucial to combat those. Some things that tend to help are related to reconnecting with the feelings in your body: taking walks in nature (with bare feet for grounding to the Earth), doing gentle yin yoga, and Somatic Experiencing, a therapy that works through body sensations.

items.title: 1. Your method in the parts people use in trouble: how?
items.question:
A fresh reader found 15 places where the guide gives generic advice where your method would change what the reader or helper does ([where](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/claude/bad-trips-20261105/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h37-20261108/beliefs/GENERIC.md)). Your first five minutes, your don'ts and your aftermath list now carry it, which leaves 10: the sitter's script, Alone at 3 a.m., the helper's Do list, the Grounding Menu's hand on the heart and breath line, the thinking traps, Give the Session's preparation, Abuse Memories' step after sleep, Shadow Thoughts' in-trip move, and the questions after the aftermath list.

A (my pick): I move or quote sentences the guide already has, where it gives your method, into those places, one approve card each, starting with the four that matter most: Alone at 3 a.m. (someone with no sitter: "Can I send love to the one who's suffering?" and the hand on the heart), the breath line ("I can love the part of me that feels it."), Give the Session's preparation ("So train before you need it, sending love to a frightening image ...") and the thinking traps ("young parts of you that are still waiting for love ..."). Pro: your method where it's used, in sentences the guide already has, quick for you to approve. Con: a moved sentence can need a joining word, and the places read AI now, so they may still need your hand for Pangram.

B: teaching cards, one or two places at a time, for you to write each with your method in it. Pro: your voice and your view, and they read Human. Con: your time, ten places.

C: leave them. Pro: no work. Con: the guide stays generic where it's used.

items.title: 2. The Fear/Panic Loop, now that your first five minutes has it
items.question:

Pro: said once, in your words, with your view of what helps. Con: it drops four quick steps someone alone might use, and two protected warnings ("Stop debating ..." and "Repeat ...") and one of the four places your room-first order appears go with it.

B: keep only the four steps, moved right under your panic-loop paragraph, with the "ladder" said as the order it is and each line said as the person's or the helper's. items.title: 3. What Kind of Aftermath Is This?: how much of it?
items.where: What Kind of Aftermath Is This?, P1
items.question:
A (my pick): keep all eight kinds as your version has them, with the three terms on the first card and the Syrian rue question settled. Pro: each kind now says what to do and why, with your remedies, and it read High as you wrote it. Con: it's long (about 520 words), and two kinds, visual distortions and paranoia, are medical enough that the reader also needs the call-for-help lists at the top.

B: keep the five kinds a reader can recognize in themselves (anxiety and fear, sleep, shame, existential shock, bodily restlessness) and move visual distortions, derealization and paranoia to "Bring in mental-health support when:", each with your remedy in a line. Pro: shorter, and the three that may need a professional sit with the call-for-help lines. Con: it splits your version, and those remedies move away from the days-after list where the reader looks.

C: cut the list to its first paragraph and point to the sections that cover each kind. Pro: shortest. Con: loses your remedies and the days-after view.

items.title: 5. Syrian rue in your paranoia line: a safety point
items.where: What Kind of Aftermath Is This?, P7
items.question:
Your paranoia line names "the relatively safe and natural antipsychotics mentioned in this guide, like DMSO, syrian rue OIL, and niacin". The guide doesn't mention Syrian rue anywhere else, and its serotonin syndrome section lists "harmala/ayahuasca-type MAOI exposure" among the things to stop. Syrian rue (Peganum harmala) is the classic harmala source: its seed extracts strongly inhibit MAO-A, mainly through harmaline and harmine, and that inhibition is the main cause of its toxic effects ([a review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3841998/)). Someone with lingering paranoia may still be on an antidepressant or an MDMA-type drug, the combination the guide warns about.

A (my pick): say what "syrian rue OIL" is (if it's an oil used on the skin or by smell, as your capitals suggest, say so), and add the harmala warning where it's named: not with antidepressants, MDMA, other MAOIs or the rest of the serotonin list. Pro: keeps your remedy with what a reader needs to use it safely. Con: a few more words in your line.

B: take Syrian rue out of the line until it has its own place in the guide, with its warning. Pro: the safest wording now. Con: your remedy goes for now.

C: keep the line as it is. Con: it names a remedy the guide never explains, next to a warning against it.

Also, in the bodily-restlessness line, "my trusty relaxing herbs and natural antipsychotics listed above": no herbs are listed above it. Name them, or point to "Mental Stabilizers That Don't Abort the Trip".
items.comment:
a. oh shoot that's not in my guide? 

Syrian rue can be mixed into warm/hot oil (like coconut oil), just enough to cover it, then squeezed out thru cheese cloth. Within some minutes of the seeds soaking in oil (if it's hot, or maybe an hour if it's warm), the oil contains the oil-soluble harmalas, not harmine, harmaline, or THH in quantities that could make it a potent MAOi (unless one extracts with hexane and then eats a 1-2tbsp of that extract). These oil-soluble harmalas have no effect when eaten, but when absorbed thru mucous membranes or vaped, they chill out psychedelic trip intensity, making them more gentle and sweet. On their own, they have some mild psychedelic properties though (like I felt like half of my head was sort of transparent), and significant mood boosting properties. 

I have a friend with schizophrenia would would use about 1-2mL of this oil rectally when he was in psychosis, which helped at least as much as niacin an DMSO, equally effective as Geodon, an antipsychotic his doctors prescribed which makes him feel like a zombie.

Another option is vaping the whole syrian rue seeds, as it seems that these oil soluble harmalas are concentrated on the outside of the seeds. Once ground up, vaping the powder is more stimulating, less relaxing (but variable since all is mixed together). However, if vaping the whole seeds, I would not assume there's no MAOi effect (even though it still seems to reduce DMT effects) since depending maybe on temperature and time, you might also vaporize the harmine and harmaline. 

 Make sure that is in the sections it needs to be in. 

As for the relaxing herbs, I was thinking i had listed them recently. But like beach morning glory/railroad vine (Ipomoea pes-caprae), syrian rue oil, the metta nmt sniffer (did i not add that?), or if they don't have that, just AUTHENTIC natural calming esesntial oils to smell like rose geranium, jasmine, lemon/lime oils. Most of these oils are fake on amazon so buy only directly from trusted essential oil vendors. It should not smell like a perfume. Even just taking a lime and scratch & sniff the peel can be relaxing. 

Smelling humic acid powder is also very good for relaxation and mental clarity. I think i mentioned that in various places.
